title: Analysis of thymoquinone content in black cumin seeds using near-infrared reflectance spectroscopy
content: Thymoquinone (TMQ) is the main therapeutic constituent in black cumin (Nigella sativa L.) seeds. Conventional quantification by high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) is accurate but unsuitable for large-scale screening. This study evaluated the potential of near-infrared reflectance spectroscopy (NIRS) as a rapid and non-destructive alternative. A multiyear dataset of 780 seed samples was analyzed, and robust calibration models were developed using modified partial least squares regression. Independent validation of a two-year calibration equation with samples from a third year revealed a high predictive performance (r² = 0.85; SEP = 1.18 mg g-¹), which was further improved by adding up to 50% of the samples of the third year in the model (r² = 0.88; SEP = 1.01 mg g-¹). Calibration equations proved highly effective for selecting genotypes with high TMQ content, with up to 100% match at the top 5% selection intensity. Spectral analysis identified key wavelengths associated with TMQ content, with wavelengths around 2106 nm and 2254 nm being the most relevant. This work demonstrates the applicability of NIRS for rapid phenotyping of TMQ content in black cumin seeds.
